questions.q: Find the least number which when divided by 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 leaves the remainder 3 in all cases.
questions.solution: LCM(4,6,8,10,12)=120. Add the common remainder 3 to obtain 123 among the options.

questions.q: In a factory, 60% of the workers are above 30 years and of these 75% are males and the rest are females. If there are 135 male workers above 30 years, the total number of workers in the factory is
questions.solution: Men above 30 are 60%×75%=45% of all workers. Total = 135/0.45=300.

questions.q: A 20% reduction in the price of an apple enables a man to buy 10 apples more for ₹54. Then what is the reduced price of apples per dozen ?
questions.solution: A 20% price reduction raises the quantity by 25%. The additional 10 apples imply an original quantity of 40 and a new quantity of 50. New price per dozen = 54/50×12=₹12.96.

questions.q: In a glass, milk and water are mixed in the ratio of 3: 5 and in another glass they are mixed in the ratio of 6: 1. In what ratio should the contents of the two glasses be mixed together so that the new mixture contains milk and water in the ratio of 1:1?
questions.solution: Milk fractions are 3/8 and 6/7, with target 1/2. Alligation gives first:second=(6/7−1/2):(1/2−3/8)=20:7.

questions.q: The cost price of 72 books is equal to the selling price of 60 books. What is the gain percent?
questions.solution: Selling price per book divided by cost per book is 72/60=1.2. The profit is 20%.

questions.q: If bananas are bought at the rate of 60 for 50 and sold at the rate of 50 for ₹60, what is the profit percent?
questions.solution: Cost per banana is 50/60 and selling price is 60/50. Their ratio is 1.44, giving 44% profit.

questions.q: Find the LCM of 12, 18, 20, 25.
questions.solution: Take the highest prime powers: 2²×3²×5²=900.

questions.q: A can do a certain job in 120 days. B is 60% more efficient than A. To do the same job B alone would take how many days?
questions.solution: B’s rate is 1.6 times A’s rate. B’s time = 120/1.6=75 days.

questions.q: A woman borrowed 25,220 and she returned the money in three equal instalments after one, two and three years. If the rate of compound interest is 5%, then find the value of each instalment.
questions.solution: Let each instalment be E. Discount them to the borrowing date: E/1.05+E/1.05²+E/1.05³=25220. This gives E=₹9261.

questions.q: A takes 50% more time to complete a work than B. If together they take 27 days to complete the work, how much time shall B take to do it alone?
questions.solution: Let B take t days; A takes 1.5t. Their joint rate is 1/t+2/(3t)=5/(3t)=1/27. Hence t=45 days.

questions.q: A sum of₹ 3,000 amounts to ₹ 6,000 in two years at compound interest. The interest for four years is
questions.solution: The amount doubles every two years. After four years it is ₹12,000, so interest is ₹12,000−₹3,000=₹9,000.

questions.q: After giving a discount of 12% on the marked price of a book, a shopkeeper earns a profit of 21%. If he doesn't give this discount, then how much profit would he earn?
questions.solution: Selling at 88% of marked price yields 121% of cost. Marked price is 121/88=137.5% of cost, so the undiscounted profit is 37.5%.

questions.q: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on the marked price of a camera. If the cost price of the camera is 3,600, find the marked price so that shopkeeper can earn a profit of 20%, after allowing 10% discount.
questions.solution: Required selling price = 3600×1.20=₹4320. This is 90% of marked price, giving marked price ₹4800.

questions.q: A, B and C entered into a partnership, and their investment ratio was 5: 4:3. After 4 months, B invested 1,000 more and after 8 months, C invested 2,000 more. At the end of one year, if the profit ratio was 15: 14: 11, then find the investment of C at the beginning.
questions.solution: Initial investments are 5k,4k,3k. Weighted capital-times are 60k,48k+8000,36k+8000. Comparing B with A using 14:15 gives k=1000. C initially invested 3k=₹3000.

questions.q: In a partnership, X invests $\frac{1}{6}$th of the capital for $\frac{1}{6}$th of the time, Y invests $\frac{1}{3}$rd of the capital for $\frac{1}{3}$rd time and Z invests the remaining capital for the whole time. If at the end of the year the profit earned is ₹23,000, then what will be Y's share?
questions.solution: Capital-time products are 1/36,1/9,1/2, giving profit ratio 1:4:18. Y receives 4/23 of ₹23,000=₹4000.

questions.q: If a, b, c, d, e are five consecutive odd numbers, then their average is
questions.solution: The numbers are a,a+2,a+4,a+6,a+8. Their average is the middle term a+4.

questions.q: Of the three numbers, the second is twice the first and thrice the third. If the average of the three numbers is 44, the largest number is
questions.solution: Let the second number be 6k. The first is 3k and third 2k. Their sum is 11k=132, giving k=12 and largest number 72.

questions.q: In a 2025 litre mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk to water is 12: 13. To get a new mixture containing milk and water in the ratio of 12: 15, the amount of water to be added is
questions.solution: Milk is 2025×12/25=972 litres and water is 1053. At ratio 12:15, water must be 972×15/12=1215. Add 1215−1053=162 litres.

questions.q: In an office, 30% of the staff is female. 60% of the female staff and 40% of the male staff are married. The percentage of the unmarried staff in the office is
questions.solution: Married staff = 30%×60%+70%×40%=46%. Unmarried staff = 54%.

questions.q: Walking $\frac{3}{4}$th of her normal speed, Athira is 15 minutes late in reaching her office. What is the usual time taken by her to cover the distance between her home and office?
questions.solution: At three-quarters speed, time becomes four-thirds of normal. The extra one-third equals 15 minutes, so normal time is 45 minutes.

questions.q: The captain of a cricket team of 11 members is 29 years old, and the wicket-keeper is four years older than the captain. If the ages of the captain and the wicket-keeper are excluded, the average age of the remaining players of the team is two years less than the average age of the whole team. What is the average age of the team?
questions.solution: Let team average be x. Captain and wicketkeeper total 29+33=62. Then 11x−62=9(x−2), so 2x=44 and x=22.

questions.q: What is the probability of drawing an ace from a pack of 52 cards?
questions.solution: A standard deck has four aces in 52 cards. Probability = 4/52=1/13.

questions.q: What is your final position in relation to your starting point if you have walked 10 km South, then turned 90 degrees to the left and walked another 6 km ?
questions.solution: The paths are perpendicular: 10 km south and 6 km east. Distance = √(100+36)≈11.66 km, matching the 11.6 km option.

questions.q: In a survey, 60% of people preferred Option A and 40% preferred Option B. If there were a total of 500 respondents, how many of them preferred Option A?
questions.solution: Number preferring A = 60%×500=300.

questions.q: In a class of 40 students, 20 have chosen only Biology and 15 have chosen Mathematics, but not Biology. Given that every student has chosen either Mathematics, or Biology, or both. Find the number of students who chose both Mathematics and Biology.
questions.solution: The disjoint groups are Biology only, Mathematics only and both. Both = 40−20−15=5.
